DECREMENT - Decrement is the act of decreasing or becoming less. When something is subtracted or lost it is decremented. For example: If the number 5 is decremented by 1, the remaining number is 4. If the binary number 0011 is decremented by 1, the remaining number is 0010.
DEFINITION

Down counters count in one of two modes of operation: Free Run or Single Step.
In free run mode, the counter counts from the maximum count to zero and then starts the count over.
FREE RUN - Example: A MOD 8 counter has a maximum count of 7. A down counter will count down from 0111 to 0000, then reset to 0111 and start the count again.
A MOD10 counter has a maximum count of 9. A down counter will count down from 1001 to 0000, then reset to1001 and start the count over..
In free run mode, the counter counts from the maximum count to zero and then starts the count over.
Each input pulse is counted and subtracted from the current count. The count continues down to 0000.
At count 0000, the next input pulse sets the counter to the maximum count and the counting starts over.
In single step mode, the counter counts from the maximum count to zero and stops.
Each input pulse is counted and subtracted from the current count. The count continues down to 0000.
At count 0000, the input pulses are disabled inside the counter. The counter stops counting.
This counter stops when the count is 000. What mode of operation is used?
In the free run mode, the counter decrements from its maximum count to zero and starts the count again. The counter does not stop.
TRY AGAIN!
This is a MOD 8 counter, but the mode is either free run or single step.
TRY AGAIN!
This counter counts from the maximum count to 0000 and starts over. What mode of operation is used?
In the single step mode, the counter decrements from its maximum count to zero and stops.
TRY AGAIN!
This is a MOD 10 counter, but the mode is either free run or single step.
TRY AGAIN!

Input pulses are applied to the clock input. As the pulses enter the counter they are counted.

CLOCK INPUT - Down counters use a basic synchronous input pulse circuit.
Synchronous means that the flip-flops are connected to a common input such that each flip-flop will be triggered at the same time.
The Enable input, when low, allows the counter to function. A high disables the counter.
ENABLE INPUT - A low enable input is inverted and applied to the J and K inputs of each flip-flop. This places the flip-flops in the toggle mode of operation.
A high enable input applies a 0 on the J and K inputs. This disables the flip-flops. The counter will not count..............
The Enable input, when low, allows the counter to function. A high disables the counter.
The Load input determines what number will start the counter. A low starts the counting again.
When the Load input goes low, the counter sets to the binary number on inputs A through D.
When the Load input goes low, the counter sets to the binary number on inputs A through D.
LOAD INPUT - Recall that a low is required on PRE and CLR inputs to override the clock input.
When the load input is low, a high is applied to both AND gates............................................................
If input A is a 1, a low is applied to the PRE input and the flip-flop sets. A high is applied to the CLR input...............
If input A is a 0, a low is applied to the CLR input and the flip-flop resets. A high is applied to the PRE input.............
QA through QD or QA through QD are outputs. These outputs are sent to a logic gate that determines when the Load input will set the counter.
CIRCUIT OUTPUTS - In this example, the Q outputs are connected to a NAND gate. When the count is 1111, the output is low.
The low output of the NAND gate triggers the load input. The counter sets to the number from inputs A through D...............
QA through QD or QA through QD are outputs. These outputs are sent to a logic gate that determines when the Load input will set the counter.

This counter circuit counts up or down in free run or single step modes and is capable of producing various MODs.
As an up counter the Up/Down input must be grounded. The logic gate used is an AND gate.
As a down counter the Up/Down input requires 5 volts. The logic gate used is a NOR gate.
On any count other than 0000, a low is applied to the Enable input. This allows the counter to count.
The low applied to the flip-flop places a high on the Load input. The data in the register is prevented from loading.
The counter counts down to 0000. This places a high on the Enable input and the counter stops counting.
The high from the NOR gate sets the flip-flop producing a low output to the Load input.
The low on the Load input allows the contents of the register to be loaded into the counter. This sets the MOD.
With 1111 in the counter, the counting starts again. starts again.
In the single step mode, the flip-flop is disabled. The counting stops until S1 is pressed to load the counter.

Note, the output of the NOR gate will not load the register with 1111. This counter is operating in single step mode.

Note, the output of the NOR gate loads the register with 1010. This counter is operating in the free run mode.
